subject: physics

unit.name: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
question_text: Define angular acceleration and torque. Establish the relation between angular acceleration and torque.

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), Unit 7 SHORT ANSWER. The mark split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher; no exam appearance years are printed, so appearances[] stays empty.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: Angular acceleration
lines: the rate of change of angular velocity.
steps.margin_note: Definition, formula, unit — one mark, three short lines.
steps.why: α completes the rotational alphabet: θ, ω, α mirror s, v, a exactly.
common_mistakes: Confusing α with ω — acceleration is the rate of change OF the velocity.

recall.must_convey: That angular acceleration is the rate of change of angular velocity, α = dω/dt.
accept: rate of change of angular velocity
alpha is d omega by d t
reject: rate of change of angular momentum

steps.memory_tip: The unit gives the definition: rad/s² is radians per second, per second.

steps.label: Torque
lines: the rate of change of angular momentum.
steps.margin_note: Give the dL/dt definition here — it is the one the derivation below starts from.
steps.why: Torque has two faces: r × F says where it comes from; dL/dt says what it does. The relation below needs the second face.
common_mistakes: Defining torque only as r × F and then having nothing to differentiate.

recall.must_convey: That torque is the rate of change of angular momentum, τ = dL/dt.
accept: rate of change of angular momentum
tau is d L by d t
reject: rate of change of angular velocity

steps.memory_tip: τ = dL/dt is the exact twin of F = dp/dt. Write it that way and the derivation is set up.

steps.label: The relation
lines: For a rigid body rotating about a fixed
axis, L = Iω with I constant, so
the rotational form of F = ma.
steps.margin_note: Say WHY I comes out of the derivative — the body is rigid, so I is constant. That one clause is the derivation.
steps.why: τ = Iα is Newton’s second law with every actor replaced by its rotational twin: force→torque, mass→moment of inertia, acceleration→angular acceleration.
common_mistakes: Pulling I out of the derivative without saying it is constant — for a rigid body it is, and saying so earns the step.

recall.must_convey: That L = Iω with constant I gives τ = Iα, the rotational F = ma.
accept: I is constant so it comes out
reject: tau is d L by d t

steps.memory_tip: Two lines only: write L = Iω, then differentiate it. Nothing else is needed.

insider_note: The relation carries 2 of the 4 marks and the two definitions one each, so all three parts must be written.
